summary: The note is a Wikipedia article on the giant-impact hypothesis, the leading explanation for lunar formation, which proposes that a Mars-sized body called Theia struck the early Earth about 4.5 billion years ago and its ejecta coalesced into the Moon. It covers the history of lunar-origin theories from George Darwin through Daly, Hartmann and Davis, and Cameron and Ward, the supporting evidence (isotopes, angular momentum, density, zinc), the remaining difficulties (volatile depletion, iron oxide content, lack of a Venusian moon), and alternative hypotheses such as the late asteroid impact and the Canup co-formation model.
one_line: Wikipedia overview of the giant-impact hypothesis, which holds that a Mars-sized body named Theia collided with early Earth and formed the Moon.
key_facts: The giant-impact hypothesis was first proposed in 1946 by Canadian geologist Reginald Daly, according to the article's lead section.
The hypothesis suggests Early Earth collided with a Mars-sized dwarf planet approximately 4.5 billion years ago, and the ejecta later accreted to form the Moon.
The impactor is sometimes called Theia, a name proposed initially by English geochemist Alex N. Halliday in 2000.
At the 1969 conference at Kona, Hawaii, the giant-impact hypothesis emerged as the most favored hypothesis for lunar origin.
In 2001, a team at the Carnegie Institution of Washington reported that Apollo rocks had an isotopic signature identical with rocks from Earth.
In 2014, a team in Germany reported that the Apollo samples had a slightly different isotopic signature from Earth rocks, a difference that was slight but statistically significant.
In 2007, researchers from the California Institute of Technology showed that the likelihood of Theia having an identical isotopic signature as Earth was very small (less than 1 percent).

The Moon's iron oxide (FeO) content of 13% is intermediate between Mars (18%) and the terrestrial mantle (8%), which the article says rules out most of the proto-lunar material coming from Earth's mantle.
Estimates suggest some twenty percent of the original mass of Theia ended up as an orbiting ring of debris around Earth, and about half of this matter coalesced into the Moon.
Zinc isotope comparisons show Moon rocks contain more heavy zinc isotopes and less zinc overall than Earth or Mars rocks, consistent with evaporative depletion during a giant impact.
The article reports that the lunar core radius is less than about 25% of the Moon's radius, in contrast to about 50% for most other terrestrial bodies.
A 2019 model proposed that about 80% of the Moon-forming debris originated from the proto-Earth, while many prior models had suggested 80% came from the impactor.
Analysis of the Moon's titanium isotope ratio (50Ti/47Ti) shows it is within 4 ppm of Earth's, suggesting little if any of the colliding body's mass could have been part of the Moon.
In 2012, Robin M. Canup proposed that the Moon and Earth formed together from a collision of two planetary bodies, each larger than Mars, which then re-collided to form Earth.

entities.name: Reginald Aldworth Daly
entities.role: Harvard University scientist who in 1946 adjusted George Darwin's explanation to propose that an impact, not centrifugal forces, created the Moon

entities.name: George Darwin
entities.role: Proposed in 1898 that Earth and the Moon were once a single body, with the Moon spun from Earth by centrifugal forces

entities.name: Theia
entities.role: Hypothesized Mars-sized protoplanet that struck early Earth and whose ejecta formed the Moon

entities.name: William K. Hartmann
entities.role: Co-author with Donald R. Davis of a 1975 Icarus paper on satellite-sized planetesimals and lunar origin

entities.name: Donald R. Davis
entities.role: Co-author with William K. Hartmann of a 1975 Icarus paper on satellite-sized planetesimals and lunar origin

entities.name: Alastair G. W. Cameron
entities.role: Canadian astronomer who with William R. Ward suggested the Moon formed from a tangential impact of a Mars-sized body

entities.name: William R. Ward
entities.role: American astronomer who with Alastair G. W. Cameron suggested the Moon formed from a tangential impact of a Mars-sized body

entities.name: Alex N. Halliday
entities.role: English geochemist who initially proposed the name Theia in 2000

entities.name: Andreas Reufer
entities.role: Physicist at the University of Bern whose 2012 simulations supported a direct collision hypothesis

entities.name: Robin M. Canup
entities.role: Author of a 2012 model proposing the Moon and Earth formed together from a double collision

entities.name: Edward Belbruno
entities.role: Princeton University mathematician who in 2004 proposed with J. Richard Gott III that Theia coalesced at a Lagrangian point

entities.name: J. Richard Gott III
entities.role: Astrophysicist who in 2004 proposed with Edward Belbruno that Theia coalesced at an L4 or L5 Lagrangian point

entities.name: Bill Hartmann
entities.role: Lunar scientist who with Roger Phillips and Jeff Taylor challenged lunar scientists to make up their minds before the 1969 conference

entities.name: Carnegie Institution of Washington
entities.role: Institution whose team in 2001 reported Apollo rocks had an isotopic signature identical to Earth rocks

entities.name: California Institute of Technology
entities.role: Institution whose researchers in 2007 showed the likelihood of Theia having an identical isotopic signature was less than 1 percent

entities.name: University of Bern
entities.role: Institution where physicist Andreas Reufer and colleagues ran simulations supporting the direct collision hypothesis

entities.name: University of Münster
entities.role: Institution whose 2019 team reported the molybdenum isotopic composition of Earth's mantle originates from the outer Solar System

entities.name: Spitzer Space Telescope
entities.role: Detected warm silica-rich dust and SiO gas around the star HD 172555 in the Beta Pictoris moving group

entities.name: GRAIL mission
entities.role: Mapping mission that the article says has ruled out the scenario of a lunar collision with a smaller body causing hemispheric differences

entities.name: Kona, Hawaii
entities.role: Location of the October 1969 conference on lunar origins where the giant-impact hypothesis emerged as the favored hypothesis

entities.name: Synestia
entities.role: Doughnut-shaped transient object proposed in a 2018 model as a rapidly spinning pre-Earth body that later formed Earth and the Moon
